title: Portable Run Record
description: Captures one subagent run. Harness-agnostic — each harness writes an adapter from its native transcript format to this shape. Downstream grading reads only this file.

eval_id.description: Matches the eval's id in evals.json.

condition.description: Reserved names: with_skill, without_skill, old_skill, new_skill.

skill_path.description: Absolute path to the SKILL.md the subagent could load, or null if no skill was provided (without_skill condition).

prompt.description: The user prompt as dispatched to the subagent.

files.description: Fixture files the subagent had access to (absolute paths inside the run's workspace).

final_message.description: The agent's final user-facing text output.

tool_invocations.description: Ordered list of tool calls during the run.

name.description: Tool name as recorded by the harness (e.g. Bash, Read, run_command). Adapters should preserve original names.

args.description: Tool arguments. Object for structured tools, string for raw command-style tools.

result.description: Tool output, if captured. Truncate long outputs to ~2KB.

ordinal.description: 0-indexed position in the run. Used by must_precede checks.

total_tokens.description: From the harness's task completion event, or derived from the persisted transcript by record-runs using harness-specific normalization. Canonical timing lives in the sibling timing.json, whose `source` field records which origin produced it. May be null if neither source is available.

duration_ms.description: From the harness's task completion event, a native duration field, or enough persisted transcript timestamps to derive wall-clock time. Canonical timing lives in the sibling timing.json. May be null when the harness does not expose reliable timing.

run_index.description: 1-based run index within a multi-run (eval, condition) cell; absent for single-run cells.

conversation.description: Ordered multi-turn evidence and scripted-delivery outcome. Absent for one-shot runs.

codebase.description: The codebase this run's environment was built from. Absent for a fixture-only run.

skill_source.description: The skill under test this run staged, as the run resolved and copied it. Absent for a record written before skills were sourced.

kind.description: Whether the codebase came from a repository URL or a directory on the host that ran it.

source.description: The url or path exactly as declared in evals.json.

resolved_path.description: Absolute directory a path source resolved to on the host that ran it.

ref.description: Declared branch, tag, or commit SHA, for a git source.

revision.description: The commit the run actually ran against. A declared ref does not identify this on its own, because a branch moves. Absent only for a directory carrying no history.

origin_url.description: The source repository's origin. For a host-local path this is the only handle another reader can resolve: origin_url plus revision names the same tree anywhere.

branch.description: Branch the task environment was checked out on.

host_local.description: True when the source cannot be resolved off the host that ran it, so a published claim citing it is not reproducible from the eval config alone.

dirty.description: True when the copy this record describes carries uncommitted work from its source, so revision alone does not name what ran. A codebase is checked out at a commit and is never dirty; a skill is copied as it sits on disk and can be.

kind.description: How the skill was named. A skill is named by a path on the host that ran it.

source.description: The skill directory exactly as it was resolved from.

resolved_path.description: Absolute skill directory on the host that ran it. This is the pointer promote-baseline writes its baseline back through.

ref.description: Declared ref, for a source named by one.

revision.description: The commit of the repository holding the skill. Absent when the skill is in no repository.

origin_url.description: The skill repository's origin. For a host-local path this is the only handle another reader can resolve: origin_url plus revision names the same tree anywhere.

branch.description: Branch the skill repository was on.

host_local.description: True when the skill cannot be resolved off the host that ran it, so a published claim citing it is not reproducible from a path alone.

dirty.description: True when the copy this record describes carries uncommitted work from its source, so revision alone does not name what ran. A codebase is checked out at a commit and is never dirty; a skill is copied as it sits on disk and can be.

siblings.description: Sibling skills staged alongside the skill under test, as the roster was captured at resolution.
